context_documents.title: 2025-1778 · Game simulation preceded the ground-intake commitment
context_documents.body:
# 2025-1778: Game simulation preceded the ground-intake commitment

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A narrow initial ground concept became a wide collector, feeding an internally belted elevator and arm that can score toward either side. The team reports offseason experience with similar mechanisms. Each software state specifies the collector, elevator, arm and roller setpoints together, with explicit transition conditions.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team describes running match simulations on day two after kickoff to test the significance of unprotected station defense. It connects the floor collector to that strategic result and the monolithic state structure to predictable safe motion.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

This is a process reference as much as a hardware reference. The team tested a game constraint before committing to a cycle architecture, then used known mechanism families to reduce development risk. Wide acquisition helps only when the handoff can keep up and the arm can safely retract past both field and robot structure. A multi-subsystem state should retain possession information so a timing variation does not silently drop coral.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Repeat the strategic simulation with plausible opposing and partner robots. Test interrupted transfers and safe recovery from each intermediate state, rather than validating only the nominal score sequence.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

source_reviews.title: SubZero CAD and code release
source_reviews.locator: Posts 1–2 and replies on arm encoder, line breaks and stepped shafts
source_reviews.review_basis: Read team's release and detailed replies.
facts: Stationary lower axle is essential to handoff and was restrained with tape. A 2.22 encoder ratio distinguishes arm positions in a software window of ±290 degrees from down. Encoder is used for initialization. Small round bearings and machined shafts compact the gearboxes.
source_reviews.limitations: Code and CAD linked, with no independent dimensional or full state-machine audit.

source_reviews.title: Chill Out reveal and retained dossier
source_reviews.review_basis: Read older synopsis for game simulation, structure and controls.
facts: Ground supply, wide collector and automatic transfer were retained as architecture context.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: SubZero couples floor acquisition to a rotating elevator-mounted arm that can score to either side. That makes a normal pickup a coordinated motion rather than just a roller command. The release exposes two details that decide whether the architecture works in practice: the lower axle must remain fixed for transfer, and the arm must know its winding state at startup even when two positions look identical to an observer.
piece_flow: Collect coral from the floor, index it for an elevator/arm handoff,
move the gripped pipe to the chosen side of the reef. The retained synopsis describes an automated transfer involving the intake, elevator, arm and rollers.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: Bidirectional scoring reduces some chassis turns, but adds arm sweep and cable-wrap constraints. The intake loading pose and scoring-to-stow transitions must clear the structure, bellypan and reef. A sensor that reports angle modulo one revolution cannot by itself distinguish the two physical winding states.

subsystems.name: Collector and handoff
subsystems.construction: Wide floor collector and internally belted elevator per retained dossier. The team release confirms a fixed bottom axle secured in practice with tape.
subsystems.operation: Hold the intake in a usable loading geometry while the arm and elevator receive the coral.
subsystems.team_rationale: Prior synopsis attributes the move to ground supply to station defense identified in a mock game.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Even a nominally stationary axis needs positive torque retention. An axle that creeps can change handoff without a visible broken roller, so prototype it under repeated reversible torque.
subsystems.interfaces: Intake axle, guide geometry, arm load pose and sensor triggers set handoff repeatability.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Mark the axle to observe slip and test a mechanical anti-rotation feature at worst-case assembly clearance.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact axle function, handoff timing and worn-piece tolerance.

subsystems.name: Arm winding and initialization
subsystems.construction: Reduced, noninteger absolute-encoder drive and software travel bounds, as described by team.
subsystems.operation: Resolve the physical starting wrap state, then track the arm within the wiring limit while selecting reachable poses.
subsystems.team_rationale: Team selected the ratio to distinguish equal arm angles in different allowed wraps.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: An encoder reduction trades range against angular resolution at the arm and makes backlash matter at initialization. Validate restart while the arm is between common park positions.
subsystems.interfaces: Motion controller needs the correct initial arm reference before it can enforce wire or structure limits.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test boots on both sides of the wrap boundary and with a sensor fault. Check actual cable strain near the software limits.
subsystems.unknowns: Runtime fallback after loss of relative tracking or initialization error.

subsystems.name: Sensing and service
subsystems.construction: Through-hole line breaks mounted to nut strips and compact machined-shaft gearboxes in release replies.
subsystems.operation: Use sensor transitions to confirm the piece path while retaining compact mechanical interfaces.
subsystems.team_rationale: Team notes practical mounting difficulty and would consider alternate sensors.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A compact gearbox saves space near the arm, but a replacement sensor needs access and an unambiguous reference after service.
subsystems.interfaces: Sensor mounting, wire routing and state transitions must agree.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inject blocked or disconnected sensors during transfer. Time replacement without removing the main elevator.

revisions: Retained record identifies wider floor intake replacing an early concept. Release documents the fixed axle and arm encoder setup.
transferable_principles: Require explicit anti-rotation for functionally fixed shafts.
Separate displayed joint angle from absolute cable winding state.
disconfirming_conditions: A constrained single-sided arm may save more cycle time if drive heading is already consistent.
Wide pickup adds limited benefit with reliable protected station access.
remaining_gaps: Actual source-file audit, endgame, event changes and complete captions.
